newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia '96 oil products output growth at 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia '96 oil products output growth at 10 pct.

text.p: Malaysia's total output of petroleum products is expected to grow at a slower pace of 10 percent this year, after increasing by a sharp 18.5 percent last year, the Ministry of Finance said on Friday.
The moderation is due to the limitations of refining capacities as well as near stagnation in crude oil production, it said in the annual economic report.
After upgrading programmes by oil companies, total refining capacity in Malaysia is currently at 378,000 barrels per day (bpd), it said.
Another 100,000 bpd will be added after December next year when the sour crude train at the Petronas refinery in central Malacca state is completed. Petronas is the national oil company.

The report said Malaysia's output of petroleum products increased moderately by 11 percent in the first seven months of 1996 compared with end-1995 after rising by 22.4 percent during the same period of 1995.

Production of fuel oil increased by 32.7 percent in the first seven months of 1996. During the same 1996 period, output of kerosene was up 11 percent, diesel and gas oil up 6.4, liquefied petroleum gas up 13.1 and gasoline four percent.
